newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian surfactant demand to post robust growth.
newsitem.headline: Asian surfactant demand to post robust growth.

text.p: Demand in Asia for surfactant chemicals which are used extensively in the textile, detergent and cosmetic industries will post the strongest growth rates in the world, an analyst said on Monday.

Neil Moulden, who heads a British-based consultant company on the surfactant chemical industry, said at an industry conference in Singapore that Asian consumption of surfactant chemicals reached 2.9 million tonnes in 1996 against three million tonnes for North America.
"The prospects for growth are certainly excellent," he said, adding increasing affluence has led to an expansion of the surfactant market.
Moulden said Asian demand expanded by seven percent in 1996 against the one to two percent growth seen in North America and Western Europe.

Yao Qingqi, deputy general manager in China Chem, said in a report at the same conference the textile industry in China is the largest consumer of surfactant chemicals followed by the petroleum and the pesticide industry.
Demand for liquid surfactants in the detergent industry alone will rise to 50,000 tonnes by 2000 from around 15,000 tonnes in 1995, he said.
The construction of new plants to produce the chemicals should allow China to match the sharp growth in demand, he said.
Some of the surfactant chemicals are derived from palm oil and coconut oil.
